source_reviews.independent_solution: Angle means both rays plus a chosen closed region, including reflex regions. A bounded polygonal intersection of two angles has 3 or 4 vertices: convex-convex uses at most four half-planes; convex-reflex is a union of at most two bounded triangles cut from the convex wedge and sharing its apex, giving triangle or concave quadrilateral; reflex-reflex has a common unbounded direction because two excluded sectors of width <180 degrees cannot cover all directions. C={x>=0,y>=0}, R={2x+y<=3 OR x+2y<=3} gives concave quad (0,0),(3,0),(1,1),(0,3). Two triangles are convex and use at most six supporting lines, so polygonal intersections have 3,4,5,6 vertices. T1={x>=0,y>=0,x+y<=4}, T2={x<=3,y<=3,x+y>=1} gives six; relaxing y<=3 to y<=5 gives five, further relaxing x+y>=1 to >=-1 gives four, containment gives three.

source_reviews.independent_solution: A convex polygon contains every diagonal by convexity. Conversely if all vertex-pair segments are in a simple filled polygon P, every convex-hull edge is in P. Since P's exterior is connected, no exterior point inside the hull can reach infinity without crossing hull boundary in P. Thus P equals its hull and is convex. Contrapositively every nonconvex polygon has a hull edge not wholly in P, joining nonadjacent vertices, hence an external diagonal. A concave quad also has an internal diagonal, so not all diagonals must leave. Triangles have no diagonals, making all-diagonal containment vacuously true and consistent with convexity.
